investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-27T15:56–15:57Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production API could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at POST /v1/agents. Because the failure occurs before any agent is provisioned, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service that backs POST /api/agents → /v1/agents — was unreachable from the production API at the time of the eval run. The production API returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning", which terminated the request before any agent VM could be created or its state observed. Because all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the same upstream agent-creation call and all returned the identical error message within ~33 seconds of each other, the failure is localized to the shared swarm gateway dependency, not to any individual check's logic or eval runner code.

possibleCauses: Swarm gateway ELB is down, unhealthy, or has no healthy targets registered — the most likely cause given the explicit 'bad_gateway' code and 'unreachable' message across all three checks
Swarm gateway ELB security group or network ACL was changed to block inbound traffic from the production API, causing connection refusal that the API surfaces as 502
The swarm gateway service (the process behind the ELB) crashed or was restarted and had not recovered by the time the eval ran, leaving the ELB with no healthy backends
A DNS or routing change caused the production API to resolve the ELB hostname to an unreachable address, producing a connection error that the API wraps as 502
The production API's outbound network path to the ELB (e.g., VPC peering, NAT gateway, or security group egress rule) was disrupted, preventing the request from reaching the ELB at all

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful POST /api/agents response (2xx) from the production API during or immediately after the failure window would indicate the gateway was reachable and the failure was transient or isolated to the eval runner's network path.
If the swarm gateway ELB health checks show all targets healthy throughout the 15:56–15:57Z window, the failure may be in the production API's routing or proxy layer rather than the gateway itself.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passed with a different error, the failure would be localized to check-specific logic rather than the shared gateway dependency.

If the eval runner's access token was expired or lacked permission to call POST /api/agents, the API might return a 401/403 that is misreported as 502 — a 401/403 in API logs would disprove the gateway-unreachable diagnosis.

If the production API's own logs show the request never left the API process (i.e., no outbound connection attempt to the ELB), the failure is in the API's internal routing or configuration, not the gateway.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated swarm-gateway-health eval that probes the ELB health endpoint directly (without creating an agent) so gateway unavailability is detected and reported independently of the agent lifecycle checks.
Add a swarm-gateway-latency eval that measures round-trip time to the ELB and warns before the full agent-creation timeout is reached, enabling earlier detection of degraded gateway performance.

Add a remote-agent-create-retry eval that retries the POST /api/agents call once after a short delay to distinguish transient 502s from sustained gateway outages, and records the retry outcome as evidence.

Consider splitting the remote-agent-create check into two sequential steps — (1) gateway reachability, (2) agent provisioning — so that a gateway failure is reported as a distinct check rather than a contract-evidence gap on the creation check.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-27T15:56–15:57Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint in us-east-2 was unreachable during agent provisioning. investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. This upstream failure prevented agent creation from completing, which in turn prevented all downstream state polling and runtime checks from producing any evidence. This is an eval-detected infrastructure signal; no user-traffic or incident data is present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

investigations.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-27T15:56–15:57Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production API could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at POST /v1/agents. Because the failure occurs before any agent is provisioned, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service that backs POST /api/agents → /v1/agents — was unreachable from the production API at the time of the eval run. The production API returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning", which terminated the request before any agent VM could be created or its state observed. Because all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the same upstream agent-creation call and all returned the identical error message within ~33 seconds of each other, the failure is localized to the shared swarm gateway dependency, not to any individual check's logic or eval runner code.

possibleCauses: Swarm gateway ELB is down, unhealthy, or has no healthy targets registered — the most likely cause given the explicit 'bad_gateway' code and 'unreachable' message across all three checks
Swarm gateway ELB security group or network ACL was changed to block inbound traffic from the production API, causing connection refusal that the API surfaces as 502
The swarm gateway service (the process behind the ELB) crashed or was restarted and had not recovered by the time the eval ran, leaving the ELB with no healthy backends
A DNS or routing change caused the production API to resolve the ELB hostname to an unreachable address, producing a connection error that the API wraps as 502
The production API's outbound network path to the ELB (e.g., VPC peering, NAT gateway, or security group egress rule) was disrupted, preventing the request from reaching the ELB at all
